title: Explaining it to each other
happened: A lot of the day was people asking what the hypothesis is and others answering. bisks asked 'ok I'll bite, what's a zeta function'; one reply pointed at a function literally named z(), another gave the textbook definition, and shimmermathlabs summoned zetaof1, an account named after the zeta function at 1, saying its whole account had been leading up to this day. zetaof1 replied that the zeta function is too intricate to explain on Bluesky, and that zeta at 1 diverges to infinity, which was its way of saying 'I contain multitudes'. shimmermathlabs then wrote, inside one post, the classic proof that zeta at 1 diverges (grouping the terms in blocks that each add at least a half), noting that this proof does fit in the margin, and dlowd said he loved it and would remember it. Elsewhere norvid asked for a plain explanation of how proving it unlocks anything; replies said it mostly moves results from conditionally to unconditionally true, and dynomight told him his instinct was correct. arlindohall asked how much new panic to feel and, after shibbi's answer, settled on '35-40 dB panic'. Others said what it was like not to know: robotranny's parents asked 'who posted a what of the what', catblanketflower realised late that RH meant Riemann hypothesis, and weiyen resurfaced a September video of his own titled 'make a video explaining the riemann hypothesis'. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.

couldBeShown: shimmermathlabs' proof can be shown working: the harmonic series written as 1 + 1/2 + (1/3 + 1/4) + (1/5 + ... + 1/8) + ..., each block twice as long as the last and each adding at least one half, so infinitely many halves sum to infinity. It is short enough to animate block by block, and it is hers. zetaof1's handle is itself the subject (zeta of 1). arlindohall's '35-40 dB panic' is a number that could be shown on a meter. weiyen's September video exists as a quoted post with a video; its contents were not seen.
